resources.string: Water and small dissolved substances leave the glomerular capillaries and enter the capsule. Blood cells and most large proteins stay in the bloodstream.
The proximal tubule returns much of the filtered water and salts, as well as nutrients such as glucose, to the blood.
The two limbs handle water and salt differently
Water leaves the descending limb. The ascending limb moves salt into surrounding tissue but is largely impermeable to water.
Selected substances, such as hydrogen ions, may move from the blood side into the tubule. This is the opposite direction from reabsorption.
The collecting duct carries urine away
The collecting duct can reabsorb more water. The fluid that remains flows toward the renal pelvis, and then through the ureter toward the bladder.
Slowed, simplified nephron. The chapters highlight different processes; arrows, counts and timing are not clinical measurements.
